messages:
sam: Heads-up — Cust Hypernova sent a LoRA patch for their 7B variant we host. After merging I ran a quick smoke and noticed embedding drift on numeric fields and a small drop in QA F1. Can someone take a compatibility pass for int4 quant and tokenizer mapping?

nina: thanks. do we have the PR + artifact bundle?

sam: PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/hypernova-lora (private). Artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-hypernova/patch-2026-03-20. Quick eval pack attached: hypernova_qapack.json (40 prompts: numeric + doc QA + short completion).

ben: quick question — is this LoRA trained with the standard shared-vocab tokenizer or a customer-modified vocab? small remaps cause huge embed deltas.

sam: vendor said "no vocab changes" but their repo includes a tokenizer.json that has 12 extra tokens.

maya: if tokenizer differs, embeddings will shift. run token-diff and an embed-sanity run. I can run int4 quant smoke on a dedicated node.

ci-bot: CI triggered: build-merge-hypernova-lora #482 started. Logs: https://ci.redwood/build/482

maya: running quick eval now. command:
```bash
./run_quick_eval \
  --model=llama-7b-hypernova-lora \
  --quant=int4 \
  --prompts=hypernova_qapack.json \
  --batch=8 \
  --out=artifacts/hypernova_eval.json
```

eval-bot: finished quick eval (summary):
- avg latency (1 tok): 38ms (batch=8)
- QA F1: 0.76 (baseline 0.88)
- numeric-answer F1: 0.54 (baseline 0.78)
- embed cosine mean: 0.885 (baseline 0.942)
- top-k hallucination rate: +4%

nina: Oof — that's a meaningful regression. Two immediate hypotheses: tokenizer remap or LoRA weight scaling mismatch with int4 kernels.

ben: yep. steps I recommend: 1) compare tokenizer token ids for our canonical tokenizer vs theirs (token-diff). 2) run model forward with fp16 (no quant) + same LoRA merge to confirm whether regression is quant-only.

maya: token-diff output (first 6 diffs):
```
+ <|num_unit|> -> id 50295 (cust only)
+ <|usd_sym|>  -> id 50296
+ <|percent_tag|> -> id 50297
```
These are inserted in the mid-range which shifts many downstream ids.

sam: so it's a tokenizer insertion, not a LoRA math bug?

ben: likely both amplify each other. LoRA updates were trained on their tokenizer indexes. Merging into our model with a different index mapping will misalign embeddings.

nina: immediate mitigations:
- option A: remap LoRA weights to our token ids using the mapping script (fast, but risky for OOV fallback).
- option B: ask customer to regenerate LoRA with our canonical tokenizer (preferred but slower).

maya: I ran the FP16 merged model (no quant) — FP16 metrics are close to baseline: QA F1 0.86, embed cosine 0.94. So quant + tokenizer mismatch is the main culprit.

ops: tagging infra — we should not promote int4 variant for this cust until token map is resolved. @ops can we lock dedicated pool for further tests?

ops: acknowledged, reserving a node for follow-up tests.

ben: remediation plan I'd take:
1) produce a token mapping file from their tokenizer -> canonical.
2) run weight-remap script:
```python
# pseudocode
remap_lora_weights(in_lora='hypernova.lora', mapping='token_map.json', out='hypernova.remapped.lora')
```
3) smoke eval with fp16 -> then int4. If remap fixes embeds, ship remapped LoRA as interim.

nina: can someone run the remap and a quick int4 re-eval? I'll prep a short email to the customer explaining options.

maya: starting remap now (ETA ~25m). will post artifacts to s3://redwood-hypernova/remap-2026-03-20/ and re-run the same quick eval pack.

sam: thanks all. if remap improves numeric fields we can offer a stability guide: "LoRA + tokenizer alignment checklist" for customers. saves time later. :thumbsup:

eval-bot: remap+int4 quick eval done (artifacts at s3://redwood-hypernova/remap-2026-03-20/hypernova_eval_remap.json):
- QA F1: 0.84
- numeric F1: 0.75
- embed cosine mean: 0.935
- latency: 40ms

ben: that's promising. still slight delta vs baseline but within acceptable for many prod apps. I'd recommend roll forward with remapped LoRA and a follow-up ask for a canonical-tokenizer retrain.

nina: I'll draft the customer note and include suggested cert steps (tokenizer parity, quantization smoke, 40-prompt quickpack).

sam: perfect. closing loop once customer confirms. thanks everyone.
